name: Grave Protocol Arms Terminus GPA-1 'Last Rites'
description:
A single-shot break-action railgun designed for absolute maximum velocity from the shortest possible barrel. The Terminus fires a 2mm tungsten needle at Mach 12 from a 40cm barrel, achieving penetration values that exceed rifles twice its length. The weapon is designed for a single engagement philosophy — one shot, one kill, then disappear.

Grave Protocol Arms is a manufacturer that exists only as a series of encrypted procurement channels. No facility has been identified, no employees named, and no corporate registration filed in any jurisdiction. The Terminus appears on the black market at irregular intervals, always in sealed cases with no documentation beyond a serial number etched into the receiver.

Forensic analysis of recovered Terminus weapons reveals manufacturing precision that exceeds any known commercial or military standard. Whoever builds these weapons has access to equipment that is not supposed to exist outside of Tier 5 fabrication facilities.
legality: Illegal — unregistered manufacturer, prohibited weapon class
specifications:
caliber: 2mm tungsten needle
effective_range: 100-2,000 meters
rate_of_fire: Single-shot, 20-second manual reload and capacitor recharge
capacity: 1 round
weight: 4.2 kg
power_source: Integrated micro-capacitor, 1 shot per charge cycle
tactical_use: The Terminus is the weapon of choice for operators who plan meticulously and execute once. Its single-shot nature forces a discipline that multi-round weapons do not — the shooter must commit to their one opportunity. The weapon's compact size allows it to be concealed in a briefcase or tool bag, deployed in seconds, and abandoned after use. Many operators treat the GPA-1 as disposable, purchasing a new unit for each engagement.
cultural_context: The mystery surrounding Grave Protocol Arms has generated intense speculation in GLMZ's weapons community. Theories range from a rogue Arcturus skunkworks to an AI-run fabrication facility. The Terminus has become almost mythical — a weapon so perfect and so anonymous that it represents the platonic ideal of an assassination tool. Operators who have used one describe the firing experience as 'transcendent' — the recoil is minimal, the sound is a sharp crack, and the target simply ceases to exist.
known_users: Unknown — all known operators deceased or vanished
story_hooks: A Terminus serial number was cross-referenced against a partial encryption key found in a dead intelligence operative's implant. The number sequence suggests Grave Protocol Arms is using Tessera's classified serial format — implying a connection between the companies.

Three Terminus weapons were found in a shipping container at the docks, still sealed. Whoever ordered them never collected. The cases have been sitting there for two years, and the dock authority wants them gone before someone else claims them.

physical_description.visual_profile: A brutally minimalist break-action railgun that resembles a surgical instrument more than a conventional firearm. The silhouette is dominated by a severely tapered barrel that emerges from a compact receiver barely larger than a pistol grip. The overall aesthetic is skeletal and purposeful — every curve and angle justified by ballistics, nothing extraneous.
physical_description.dimensions: Total length: 52 cm | Barrel length: 40 cm | Receiver width: 8 cm | Height (mounted): 6 cm
physical_description.weight_description: Deceptively light in hand at 4.2 kg — the weight is concentrated in the barrel and receiver, creating a front-heavy balance that demands precision grip. Feels like holding compressed intent.
physical_description.primary_material: Tungsten-alloy barrel over carbon-composite receiver. Breach block machined from aerospace-grade titanium. Integration points forged steel.
physical_description.finish: Matte black titanium with brushed graphite accents. The barrel has a subtle iridescent sheen where electromagnetic coils are embedded beneath the surface — visible only under direct light as faint interference patterns. No reflective surfaces.
physical_description.color_scheme: Deep matte black primary with gunmetal gray breach mechanism. Minimal accent lighting in cold blue from the capacitor status indicator (recessed into the left receiver face).
physical_description.grip_texture: Textured polymer with embedded dissipative coating to prevent capacitor feedback. Rough, almost abrasive — designed to be gripped hard without slipping even with sweat or blood.
distinctive_features: Capacitor indicator: small LED array (blue-green) recessed into left receiver, glowing during charge cycle
Breach mechanism: exposed titanium clamshell that rotates downward for needle loading — no external lever, motion is mechanical and deliberate
Barrel porting: microscopic electromagnetic field vents are invisible to naked eye but create subtle thermal distortion signature
Serial plate: single etched line of numbers on the receiver bottom, barely legible even at close range, laser-marked rather than stamped
Accelerator coils: faint hexagonal grid pattern visible along barrel length where composite wraps around ferrous core
No safety. No selector. No accessories rails.
Integrated thumbhole that doubles as capacitor heat sink
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: No logo. No branding. A single serial number etched into the bottom of the receiver in microscopic characters: position it under magnification to read. This is the only identification the weapon carries — no 'GRAVE PROTOCOL ARMS' stamp, no manufacturer claim, nothing that could be traced.
physical_description.condition_typical: Field units show deliberate wear patterns — never battle-scarred (these weapons are rarely fired twice), but bearing evidence of hasty preparation and swift deployment. Minor holster scratches on the receiver. Occasional residual polymer dust in the breech from transportation in sealed cases. Otherwise maintained obsessively by operators who understand they have one engagement and must execute perfectly.
